Big Hair
BIG HAIR
noun (Gen X slang)
A plain descriptive phrase that became the name of a 1980s look: hair teased, permed, crimped, and fixed with clouds of hairspray (Aqua Net was the brand of the era) into great height and volume, with "mall bangs" rising above the forehead. Women wore it on television (Dynasty, 1981–89), on country-music stages, and in every high-school yearbook; men wore it in the "hair metal" bands of the mid-to-late 1980s (Poison, Mötley Crüe, Bon Jovi). The Texas quip "the higher the hair, the closer to God" is attached to it. The look collapsed under grunge in the early 1990s.

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

Big hair is what every Gen X yearbook photo is remembered for: teased bangs standing three inches tall, permed curls, and enough hairspray to hold it all in a stiff wind. Mothers, daughters, and long-haired rock bands all took part. The Christian observation is affectionate before it is serious. Scripture does not mock a woman’s hair; it honors it: "if a woman have long hair, it is a glory to her" (1Co 11:15). And God’s care reaches to every strand: "the very hairs of your head are all numbered" (Mat 10:30). Hair is a gift and caring for it is no sin. But the old joke — "the higher the hair, the closer to God" — gets the direction exactly backward, and Scripture says so gently. Peter writes, "Whose adorning let it not be that outward adorning of plaiting the hair, and of wearing of gold, or of putting on of apparel" (1Pe 3:3), "But let it be the hidden man of the heart… even the ornament of a meek and quiet spirit, which is in the sight of God of great price" (1Pe 3:4). The point is not a ban on styling but a ranking: the heart first, the hair after. And the Bible’s own crown of hair is not volume but age: "The hoary head is a crown of glory, if it be found in the way of righteousness" (Pro 16:31). A father can laugh with his daughter at Mom’s 1987 prom picture, and tell her that the hair God most admires is the gray kind, earned by a long life of walking with Him.

Webster 1828 Definition

Gen X name for the teased, permed, hairsprayed volume of 1980s fashion and hair-metal bands; Scripture calls a woman’s hair a glory (1Co 11:15) and ranks the hidden ornament of the heart above it (1Pe 3:4).

expand to see more

BIG HAIR, n. (Gen X slang, 1980s, US) Hair styled for maximum height and volume by teasing, perming, crimping, and heavy hairspray. "Her big hair barely fit in the car."

Companions: mall bangs, teased hair, the perm, the crimping iron, Aqua Net; hair band / hair metal for its male rock form.

The Texas quip: "the higher the hair, the closer to God"; the style faded before grunge’s unwashed look after 1991.

Webster 1828: HAIR, n. 1. A small filament issuing from the skin of an animal, and from a bulbous root. …

Decode for parents: a harmless fashion with a good lesson attached — God counts every hair and still looks first at the heart.

Key Scripture

1Co 11:15 — "But if a woman have long hair, it is a glory to her: for her hair is given her for a covering."

Mat 10:30 — "But the very hairs of your head are all numbered."

1Pe 3:3 — "Whose adorning let it not be that outward adorning of plaiting the hair, and of wearing of gold, or of putting on of apparel;"

1Pe 3:4 — "But let it be the hidden man of the heart, in that which is not corruptible, even the ornament of a meek and quiet spirit, which is in the sight of God of great price."

Pro 16:31 — "The hoary head is a crown of glory, if it be found in the way of righteousness."

Modern Corruption

Big hair is mostly harmless fun, but it makes height and volume the measure of beauty; Scripture honors hair as a glory and ranks the hidden ornament of the heart, and the gray head of righteousness, above it.

expand to see more

The higher the hair. The joke tied height to holiness, and it was only a joke; but the habit behind it is real. A culture that spends an hour on the bangs and no minutes on the soul has its adornment upside down. Peter does not forbid a woman to braid her hair; he forbids her to let it be her adorning (1Pe 3:3). The ornament God prizes is a meek and quiet spirit, of great price in His sight (1Pe 3:4) — and it does not wilt in the rain.

A better crown. Every big-hair photograph is now a family joke, and that is the gentle lesson of fashion: what looked glorious at the prom looks silly at the reunion. Scripture’s crown of hair does not date. The hoary head is a crown of glory when it is found in the way of righteousness (Pro 16:31), and the God who numbers every hair (Mat 10:30) loves the gray ones on the head of a faithful saint as much as the teased ones on a girl of sixteen.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Old English hær → hair → 1980s teased, permed, hairsprayed big hair → hair-metal bands → swept away by grunge (early 1990s); Scripture: the hoary head a crown of glory (Pro 16:31).

Old English hær — hair of the head or body

Early-to-mid 1980s: perms, teasing, crimping irons, Aqua Net hairspray

Television and country music: Dynasty (1981–89), the Texas quip

Mid-to-late 1980s hair metal; early 1990s grunge ends the era

Biblical hair: a glory (1Co 11:15); every hair numbered (Mat 10:30); the hoary head a crown (Pro 16:31)

"Whose adorning let it not be that outward adorning of plaiting the hair (1Pe 3:3)."
